correctness.rationale: A Hilbert–Schmidt dissipativity equality forces any imaginary eigenoperator to annihilate absorbing Krylov spaces and commute with dephaser vertex projectors. Positive shortest-path walk amplitudes then force its matrix elements on dephased sites to vanish. The full peripheral subspace is exactly supported on the joint Hamiltonian cyclic annihilator. Finite-dimension semigroup contraction excludes peripheral Jordan blocks. Sine Fourier modes and a root-of-unity sum prove the ring formula. Program checked 1,198 instances, numerical maximum error 3.109e-15.

originality.rationale: After direct comparison with published models and prior historical claims, the asserted new statement is the universal exact asymptotic equivalence for sparse Lindblad dephasers on positive-weight connected graphs. Coherent ring two-trap arithmetic is explicitly acknowledged as previously available, not an independent discovery. Le et al. 2018 gives qualitative noise suppression of dark spaces but not the evaluated general equality. Residual uncertainty persists about general quantum-Markov invariant-subspace theorems.
residual_risks: General prior theorems on invariant enclosures/peripheral subspaces of finite quantum Markov semigroups might subsume the exact equivalence; priority not exhaustively settled.

The coherent ring two-absorber formula is already strongly anticipated by Agliari et al. (2009) and a previous claim; novelty is limited to the Lindblad dephasing identification, not its Fourier computation.

value.rationale: The all-graph structural reduction converts asymptotic mixed-state quantum transport with selective dephasing to an easily computed finite-dimensional coherent cyclic-subspace projector, clarifying which site-selective noise choices eliminate long-lived dark quantum probabilities. The exact arithmetic cycle corollary illustrates a motivated physical boundary between complete and incomplete noise-assisted absorption. The theorem does not pretend equality of finite-time dynamics.
